title: The alert storm
oneLiner: A misconfigured vulnerability scanner floods the security queue with 400 false alarms. In the middle of it, a real attacker guesses an HR employee's password and heads for the payroll files.
teaching: Alert fatigue is a capacity problem. Four analysts working in order can't get through 400 alerts in a morning, so the one real alert waits for hours. AI agents look at every alert as it arrives, so the real one doesn't wait behind the noise.

noise.title: A misconfigured vulnerability scanner sets off "repeated failed sign-in" alerts on 400 servers
noise.agentReason: Every one came from the company's own vulnerability scanner, and none ended in a successful sign-in.

labels.rootCause: A password-spraying attack tried common passwords against 300 accounts from one overseas address, and Lee Chen's weak password was the one that worked
labels.attackSummary: an attacker guessed Lee Chen's password and signed in from abroad
labels.hotEvidence: a successful sign-in from abroad right after hundreds of failed guesses against many accounts
labels.ambiguousNote: In the middle of the storm, this looks like one more failed-sign-in alert. The analyst checks the account history before deciding.
labels.objectiveImpact: Payroll data for 5,000 employees, including bank details, has been copied out.
labels.undetected: No alert fired at any point.
labels.mitre: T1110.003 password spraying, T1078 valid accounts, T1039 data from network shared drive, T1567 exfiltration over web service
labels.containDone: Lee Chen's account is locked, the password reset, and every active session ended
labels.blockDone: the attacker's address is blocked at the VPN and firewall
labels.scopeSearch: other accounts the attacker got into
labels.humanPivot: Pulls the account's sign-in history and the VPN logs, one console at a time.
labels.confirmAsk: Tier-2 calls Lee to ask about the sign-in
labels.confirmReply: Lee replies: "I'm in the office, not abroad"
labels.playbook: SOAR locks the account, resets the password, and ends active sessions.
labels.rootMissingNote: Nobody checks which other accounts were targeted.
labels.fullFinding: The same address tried 300 accounts; only Lee's guess worked.
labels.fullPackage: lock Lee Chen's account, reset the password, and end sessions; block the attacker's address
labels.containPackage: lock Lee Chen's account, reset the password, and end sessions
labels.pivotTitle: Agent checks the other failed sign-ins
labels.pivotText: The same overseas address tried 300 accounts in 20 minutes.

events.title: Password spraying from one overseas address
events.summary: From one overseas address, the attacker tries a few common passwords against 300 accounts. The failures look just like the storm.

events.title: One guess works: the attacker signs in as Lee Chen
events.summary: Lee works in HR and used a weak password. The sign-in comes from abroad.

notes.reduced: Removed: port, session ID, client version, and the metadata block. Sign-in logs are small, so this source always goes to the hot tier.
